tooling: First-party openMind Hub Client (pip) with upload/download by repo_id, plus git+LFS, plus a web UI. Documented at modelers.cn/docs/zh/openmind-hub-client. This is a genuine HF drop-in: repo types are 'model', 'dataset', 'space', same as HF.
chaining: N repos per account, free. The strategic value is that it is the domestic Ascend/MindSpore hub, so it is the natural place a Chinese-ecosystem user would park multi-hundred-GB checkpoints.

extras.quota_verbatim: Not published. The community is an explicit Hugging-Face-shaped hub — models, datasets, and Spaces, plus its own client (openMind Hub Client) and library (openMind) targeting Ascend NPUs. Its contribution guide instructs 'git lfs track' for '100MB以上' files, which confirms a real LFS backend rather than a web-only uploader. No GB ceiling appears on the site or in the docs I could reach.

extras.agent_focus: New and up-and-coming competitors to Hugging Face and ModelScope, judged on the hard test the brief sets: a credible HF competitor must permit multi-TB objects and generous per-account storage, because model weights and datasets routinely run to hundreds of GB / TiB. Split into three classes — Chinese domestic hubs (HF is blocked there, so a separate ecosystem exists), Western MLOps artifact stores (W&B/Comet/ClearML/Lightning/Deep Lake), and dataset-publishing startups (Source Cooperative, Oxen, OpenDataLab). Excluded and not re-reported: Hugging Face, ModelScope, Kaggle, Civitai, Ollama, Replicate, DagsHub, OpenML, fal.ai, Baseten, Modal.

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
